title: An opaque counter library
description:
Write a small C interface around a C++ class, with an opaque handle:

```cpp
typedef struct tally tally;                         // opaque

extern "C" int32_t tally_create(const char* name, tally** out);   // name must not be null or empty
extern "C" void    tally_destroy(tally* t);                         // null is allowed
extern "C" int32_t tally_add(tally* t, int32_t amount);            // amount may be negative
extern "C" int32_t tally_value(const tally* t, int64_t* out);
extern "C" int32_t tally_name_length(const tally* t, int32_t* out);
```

Result codes: `0` success, `1` invalid argument (a null pointer, or an empty name). Inside, keep the running total as a 64-bit number and the name as a `std::string`: those details are yours to change later because callers never see them.

`tally_add` adds to the total; the total starts at 0.
hints: Define `struct tally { std::string name; int64_t total{ 0 }; };` in the implementation. The `typedef struct tally tally;` line is all callers ever see.
